title: Vaudreuil to the minister of the Marine, four cipher letters in his 1757 table, Montréal, 8, 10 and 16 Apr 1759 (ANOM COL C11A 104) and 13 Aug 1760 (C11A 105) (catalogue 1388-1391)

steps.what: Catalogue entry and vetting record read; web searches (FR/EN) on the letter and its correspondents: no decipherment; key lead C11E 10 ff.285-290v.
Six letter images and ten key-volume images fetched from the LAC image server (curl -L; 503 on 28 Oct, working 5 Nov).
Numerical sheet e001295272 of the key volume tried on the ten commonest groups: nonsense.
Numerical sheet e001295274 tried: 642 de, 163 a, 144 pour, 430 les, 673 la, 594 ce, 547 que.
All 700 entries of sheet e001295274 transcribed from 16 enlarged cell montages (uncertain cells marked).
Letter transcribed from enlarged half-spread crops (2398 groups seen, 35 clear words).
First decode with the table as read: French at once; names Amherst, Murray, Bigot, Lévis, Ristigouche.
32 table cells corrected from context (long s read as f, l/t, c/e, b/h, homophones); inserted groups above lines added to the stream.
One group re-checked on the image (f.151r line 4, 383); historical consistency: Murray's circular, Restigouche, Lévis, Bigot, Amherst's junction at Montréal.
Coverage measured from the reading: 92.4% of all groups, 96.7% of the complete ones; 3.2% legible unread; 4.5% lost in the gutter.

Neighbouring records of C11A 105 (ff.136-146, 153-155) opened: clear letters of 7 and 13 Aug 1760 name the Machault, Bienfaisant and Marquis de Malauze, d'Angeac, La Giraudais, Villemont, the goélette l'Extravagante; none repeats the cipher letter.

Second pass with the corrected key and the images: 20 more groups read (devons, lorsque, se sera décidé, poste, coûteroit, Ontario, moindre, quarante mille ...); 25 gutter-cut groups restored from visible digits; measured 95.3% (96.3% with restored).

Sibling cipher letters of the same hand (cat. 1388-1390, 1392; C11A 104, 1759) tested with the same table: 1390 reads in full (354 groups), 1389 sample reads, 1388 same groups; 1392 uses a different code and does not read.
Siblings gave one new cell (452 fret) and no reading for the 16 unread places of 1391.
Siblings transcribed whole from the LAC images: cat. 1388 (3637 groups), 1389 (1225), 1390 (354); all decode as French with the same table; 1392 does not.
Five table cells settled from the sibling letters (301 trou, 133 oit, 367 crai, 195 vrai, 613 cas) plus 452 fret; 656 left open.

Third pass on the images: the interlinear line on f.150v belongs at a caret after 'de' (a duplicate 51 removed): 'ces derniers se lassent de notre extrême indigence, il ne faut rien moins que mes soins'; 'qui[n]ze', '[Lou]isbourg' and 'aie [don]né' settle three more places.

Alphabetical sheet e001295269 of the same volume (rotated, enlarged 5x) confirms cells 473 moyen, 152 ton, 671 bateau; cell 2 reads 'campagne' (compagnie is 102): override added. No further gap closes.

Reading read as French sentences against the English translation; every paragraph builds sentences, holes are scattered. Measured with tools/stats.py: 2326 of 2424 groups (96.0%) as written, 97.0% with 25 restored gutter-cut groups; 26 legible groups unread in 9 places, 47 lost in the gutter.

Brice Dudout (Claude Opus 5.5): independent decoder (verify_dudout_20261114.py) reading only key/key274.json with key/overrides.json, run on transcription.txt: 2401 legible number groups, none without a cell; the decoded syllables align with the letters of reading.md at 97.5% (0.958 to 0.996 per folio); the larger differences are clear words, gutter-lost groups and the open groups of gaps.json, except f. 152r, where 672 672^ 51 51 494 gives 'me me t t un' and reading.md has 'me mettroit' without a mark (494 = un, a confirmed cell). README read bar recount: research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure on reading.md gives 0.937 over 1531 words; the recorded read_share 0.96 is the share of groups (tools/stats.py), not of words, so by the README the letter is under the 0.95 word bar.

Project check of PR #565 (Brice Dudout): his decoder re-run (2401 groups, none unkeyed, 97.5% of decoded letters align with reading.md); f.152r and the first seven lines of f.151v compared group by group with LAC image e000875758 (about 240 groups, all agree; the inserted 672 above the line on f.152r line 12 is on the image). The unmarked emendation on f.152r (672 672^ 51 51 494 = me me t t un, read 'me mettroit') is now marked 'me mett[roit]' in reading.md. Word measure (README read bar) on the reading body: 1383 words, 100 holes, 0.933 < 0.95; the recorded 0.96 was a share of groups. Class changed from read to read in part; every remaining gap keeps its outside blocker (binding, open codes).

Round 13 claims review: profile brought into line with NOTES. fraction_read_source 0.971 -> 0.970 with the restored groups (2351 of 2424); codes_open.tokens_open 24 -> 26 (gaps.json key f150v.23, the count check in NOTES); documents[0].read read -> read in part (outcome.class). No reading changed.

Print step: archive.org full-text search (fts) for phrases and dates of the four letters. Parkman, Montcalm and Wolfe (1884) vol. 2 ch. 23 cites 'Vaudreuil au Ministre, 8 Avril, 1759' (census of a little over 13,000 men; a translated passage matching cat. 1388 f.62r-62v, 'If the English attack Quebec ...') and '10 Avril, 1759' (matching cat. 1389 f.69r); his other quotation of 8 Apr ('infamous conduct ... his recall') is not in cat. 1388 and must be from another letter. Nothing found for 16 Apr 1759 or 13 Aug 1760, nor for the French phrases. Casgrain's Lévis collection, the RAPQ and ANOM F3 16 not read (no full text reached); Canadiana phrase search: no results.

texts.label: cat. 1391, ANOM COL C11A 105 ff.147-152, 13 Aug 1760
texts.summary: Vaudreuil reports to the minister on the eve of the capitulation: three ships and troops bound for Restigouche under d'Angeac, the frigate Machault (La Giraudais) to run the British blockade, the lake Champlain and Ontario flotillas lost, no powder or food, Amherst, Murray and the British fleet converging on Montréal, Murray's circular letter against the paper money, and a request that the King be told the colony will fall only at the last extremity.
texts.note: read_share is the README word measure on the reading body (ff.147r-152r): 1383 words, 100 holes (supplied, restored and unread), 0.933 (14 Nov 2026). The former 0.96 was the share of groups (2326 of 2424, tools/stats.py), which stays in fraction_read. research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.measure on the whole file, preamble included, gives 0.936 (Brice Dudout, PR #565: 0.937 before the f.152r emendation was marked).

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read reading.md as French sentences from f.147r to f.152r against reading_en.md. It builds one coherent war report of 13 Aug 1760 (the ships for Restigouche under d'Angeac, the Machault, the British fleet past lake Saint-François, the landing on the north shore, the flotillas of lake Champlain and Ontario, powder and food, Murray's circular against the paper money, Lévis, the request to the King). Holes are frequent on the left-hand pages (the last group of each line lost in the binding) and in 9 places of legible groups, but none leaves a sentence unreadable; the word share is 0.933, so the letter is read in part. Images not compared in this review (the 14 Nov 2026 project check compared f.152r and part of f.151v). Not a person; I did not make this reading. Replaces the solver-side review of 5 Nov 2026 (Claude Sonnet 5.5, the model that made the reading).

texts.label: cat. 1388, ANOM COL C11A 104, ff.54-66 (CABAC_PIAF_60891), 8 Apr 1759
texts.summary: Vaudreuil reports to the minister on the winter and the defence plan: famine and loss of draught animals, a British army of about 20-25 000 against Niagara, Fort Duquesne evacuated, the four points to defend (Carillon, the Belle Rivière, Niagara, La Présentation and Lake Ontario), his plan to fall back on Québec with his troops, and numbered requests for battalions, munitions and provisions.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read cat1388/reading.md as French sentences from f.54r to f.66r, checking it against cat1388/decode.txt (the syllable decode) paragraph by paragraph. It builds one coherent despatch: the famine and the loss of the draught animals, the census of the three governments (6356 + 5455 + 1313), the four points to defend numbered 1o-4o, the plan to fall back on Québec and give battle, the requests for battalions, munitions and provisions. Holes are scattered (23 groups, the longest the 10 groups on f.64r) and none leaves a sentence unreadable; a few readings are strained where the groups are kept as written ('par cette représaille j'équivale', 'car poudre, bombes, boulets', 's-in-d-re' read 'moindre'), and seven words are supplied from the sense. Independent outside check found in this review: Francis Parkman, Montcalm and Wolfe (1884), ch. 23, translates the Québec passage of f.62r-62v ('If the English attack Quebec, I shall always hold myself free to go thither myself ... give battle ... again and again') and cites this date for the census of a little over 13,000 men; both agree with this reading. Images not compared group by group in this review. Not a person; I did not make this reading. Replaces the solver-side review of 5 Nov 2026 (Claude Sonnet 5.5, the model that made the reading).

texts.note: read_share is the README word measure on cat1388/reading.md (v10_relabel.measure_text, 24 Nov 2026): 2154 words, 38 holes (unread, supplied and restored words), 0.983. The figure recorded on 5 Nov 2026 (0.994) was a share of cipher groups.

texts.label: cat. 1389, ANOM COL C11A 104, ff.68-72 (CABAC_PIAF_60892), 10 Apr 1759
texts.summary: Vaudreuil sends the minister Montcalm's letter of 27 February, a memorandum and his own plan of operations; Montcalm's opinions had become public among officers and people, and Vaudreuil, asking Montcalm to stop it, says he would otherwise arrest the officers concerned and send them to France; he has told Montcalm he is to command at Carillon.

reading_review.by: integration review of 24 Nov 2026 (AI agent, for the maintainers); not a person
reading_review.note: Read cat1389/reading.md as French sentences from f.68r to f.72r against cat1389/decode.txt. Coherent throughout: the enclosures (Montcalm's letter of 27 February, a memorandum, the plan of operations), the spread of Montcalm's opinions among officers and people, the threat to send the officers to France, the order that Montcalm command at Carillon. Holes are scattered (the 8 groups describing the memorandum on f.68v and 2 on f.70v); seven gutter-cut groups are supplied from visible digits and the sense. Outside check found in this review: Parkman, Montcalm and Wolfe (1884), ch. 23, quotes 'Vaudreuil au Ministre, 10 Avril, 1759' for 'the people are alarmed and would lose courage if my firmness did not rekindle their zeal to serve the King', which is the end of f.69r here. Images not compared in this review. Not a person; I did not make this reading. Replaces the solver-side review of 5 Nov 2026.

texts.label: cat. 1390, ANOM COL C11A 104, ff.75-76 (CABAC_PIAF_60895), 16 Apr 1759
texts.summary: Vaudreuil asks the minister to have the munitionnaire's correspondents in France replace any ship taken, supply ships, and accept freight paid in Canada at this year's rate, and presses for a supplement of provisions on which the preservation of the Colony depends.
